essential_question: How do I get my own body ready to work, and how do I know when to stop?
learning_objectives: Perform, adapt, or describe self-directed warm-up and cool-down design safely at an intensity, range, and pace the learner sets.
Explain the movement, tactical, or training principle behind self-directed warm-up and cool-down design and why it works.
Self-assess self-directed warm-up and cool-down design against stated criteria and name the next adjustment, without comparing to any other person.
success_criteria: The learner completes or fully describes the self-directed warm-up and cool-down design task using a version their body and setting allow.
The learner gives a cue, principle, tactic, or documented process rather than an unexplained result.
The learner self-assesses against the stated criteria and identifies one next adjustment.

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Run the space, surface, footwear, and equipment check, then a learner-led warm-up. Restate the stop rule before any work on self-directed warm-up and cool-down design.

Teach the cues, principle, or tactic behind self-directed warm-up and cool-down design. Demonstrate or describe it, name the critical features, and show at least one adapted version alongside the standard version — not after it.

Practise self-directed warm-up and cool-down design with feedback on cues and decisions only. Feedback addresses the movement or the choice, never the learner's body, size, or appearance. Fade prompting as control improves.
Learner applies self-directed warm-up and cool-down design in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, what they noticed, and what they would adjust.
Cool down, then in one concise response explain the key idea behind self-directed warm-up and cool-down design and name one adjustment for next session. No recording or photograph is taken.

student_activity: Learner applies self-directed warm-up and cool-down design in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, noticed, and would adjust.
formative_check: In one concise response, explain the key idea behind self-directed warm-up and cool-down design and name one adjustment for the next session.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score safe participation, skill cues, tactical reasoning, self-management, and revision. Accept any version of the task the learner’s body and setting allow as full credit. Never score body size, weight, body composition, appearance, speed alone, or comparison with another person.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the simplest version of self-directed warm-up and cool-down design — slower, smaller range, closer target, or seated — then rebuild.
Ask the learner to explain the cue or tactic behind self-directed warm-up and cool-down design before adding intensity or complexity.
Confirm the specific cue that worked, offer one varied application of self-directed warm-up and cool-down design, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable movement pattern neutrally, contrast it with the critical features, and schedule varied practice.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: pain, dizziness, breathlessness, or head impact
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Stop immediately, tell an adult, and do not resume in this session. This is never recorded as a failed attempt.
Offer the adapted, seated, solo, or described version of self-directed warm-up and cool-down design; the alternate route is full credit and is not logged as a refusal.
Require accurate independent performance or description plus explanation on a later occasion or in a different setting before marking self-directed warm-up and cool-down design mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one session. Use safe participation, skill cues, tactical decisions, self-management, personal progress against the learner’s own stated task, and self-assessment — without body-size scoring; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions separated by time or setting.
extension: Apply self-directed warm-up and cool-down design under a new constraint, in a different activity, or teach the cue to someone else — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.

Every element has a seated, supported, low-impact, and reduced-range version. A learner using a mobility aid, working from a chair, or managing a condition designs the same routine around the movements available to them, and that routine is assessed as fully equivalent.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language about bodies, ability, and effort.
Allow a pause, rest, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Check space, footwear, surface, weather, and equipment before movement.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty, head impact, or unsafe conditions and tell an adult.
Score skill, strategy, self-management, consistency, and reflection — never body size, weight, weight change, body composition, appearance, or comparison with another person.
Do not require weight, BMI, body-fat, body measurement, fitness-test norms, percentile ranks, calorie counts, or diet goals at any point.
Do not require a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as evidence; described, written, and demonstrated-to-one-adult evidence is the intended route.
Do not require performance in front of an audience, a group, or spectators.
The learner sets their own starting point; no baseline is compared to any other learner, to a norm table, or to a prior year.
inclusive_adaptation: Every element has a seated, supported, low-impact, and reduced-range version. A learner using a mobility aid, working from a chair, or managing a condition designs the same routine around the movements available to them, and that routine is assessed as fully equivalent.

guardian_safety.equipment: No specialized equipment. Optional supportive footwear.
guardian_safety.environment: Clear indoor or outdoor space free of obstacles.
guardian_safety.movement_hazards: General activity risk. Guardian confirms the space and surface are safe and agrees the stop rule with the learner before the unit.
guardian_safety.supervision_note: Guardian sets whether activity is supervised or independent for this learner and this space.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, described demonstration, or short clip supporting self-directed warm-up and cool-down design.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, cue lists, alt text, a transcript, or an adult demonstration. No lesson requires media, and no learner media is ever produced.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose body data, fitness scores, photographs, video, recordings, or comparisons with other learners. For safety-critical units, record only the guardian confirmation that was required.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice or try one safe, optional example of self-directed warm-up and cool-down design in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

learning_objectives: Perform, adapt, or describe shared rules, fair play, and safe contact limits safely at an intensity, range, and pace the learner sets.
Explain the movement, tactical, or training principle behind shared rules, fair play, and safe contact limits and why it works.
Self-assess shared rules, fair play, and safe contact limits against stated criteria and name the next adjustment, without comparing to any other person.
success_criteria: The learner completes or fully describes the shared rules, fair play, and safe contact limits task using a version their body and setting allow.
The learner gives a cue, principle, tactic, or documented process rather than an unexplained result.
The learner self-assesses against the stated criteria and identifies one next adjustment.
materials: markers or household objects for boundaries

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Run the space, surface, footwear, and equipment check, then a learner-led warm-up. Restate the stop rule before any work on shared rules, fair play, and safe contact limits.

Teach the cues, principle, or tactic behind shared rules, fair play, and safe contact limits. Demonstrate or describe it, name the critical features, and show at least one adapted version alongside the standard version — not after it.

Practise shared rules, fair play, and safe contact limits with feedback on cues and decisions only. Feedback addresses the movement or the choice, never the learner's body, size, or appearance. Fade prompting as control improves.
Learner applies shared rules, fair play, and safe contact limits in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, what they noticed, and what they would adjust.
Cool down, then in one concise response explain the key idea behind shared rules, fair play, and safe contact limits and name one adjustment for next session. No recording or photograph is taken.

student_activity: Learner applies shared rules, fair play, and safe contact limits in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, noticed, and would adjust.
formative_check: In one concise response, explain the key idea behind shared rules, fair play, and safe contact limits and name one adjustment for the next session.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score safe participation, skill cues, tactical reasoning, self-management, and revision. Accept any version of the task the learner’s body and setting allow as full credit. Never score body size, weight, body composition, appearance, speed alone, or comparison with another person.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the simplest version of shared rules, fair play, and safe contact limits — slower, smaller range, closer target, or seated — then rebuild.
Ask the learner to explain the cue or tactic behind shared rules, fair play, and safe contact limits before adding intensity or complexity.
Confirm the specific cue that worked, offer one varied application of shared rules, fair play, and safe contact limits, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable movement pattern neutrally, contrast it with the critical features, and schedule varied practice.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: pain, dizziness, breathlessness, or head impact
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Stop immediately, tell an adult, and do not resume in this session. This is never recorded as a failed attempt.
Offer the adapted, seated, solo, or described version of shared rules, fair play, and safe contact limits; the alternate route is full credit and is not logged as a refusal.
Require accurate independent performance or description plus explanation on a later occasion or in a different setting before marking shared rules, fair play, and safe contact limits mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one session. Use safe participation, skill cues, tactical decisions, self-management, personal progress against the learner’s own stated task, and self-assessment — without body-size scoring; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions separated by time or setting.
extension: Apply shared rules, fair play, and safe contact limits under a new constraint, in a different activity, or teach the cue to someone else — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.

Activities run in seated, walking, reduced-space, reduced-pace, or no-contact versions. Solo learners use wall, target, and self-pass variants; the tactical understanding, not the game size, is what is assessed.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language about bodies, ability, and effort.
Allow a pause, rest, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Check space, footwear, surface, weather, and equipment before movement.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty, head impact, or unsafe conditions and tell an adult.
Score skill, strategy, self-management, consistency, and reflection — never body size, weight, weight change, body composition, appearance, or comparison with another person.
Do not require weight, BMI, body-fat, body measurement, fitness-test norms, percentile ranks, calorie counts, or diet goals at any point.
Do not require a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as evidence; described, written, and demonstrated-to-one-adult evidence is the intended route.
Do not require performance in front of an audience, a group, or spectators.
The learner may complete the entire unit without another participant, and modifying an activity for access is itself a graded skill rather than a concession.
inclusive_adaptation: Activities run in seated, walking, reduced-space, reduced-pace, or no-contact versions. Solo learners use wall, target, and self-pass variants; the tactical understanding, not the game size, is what is assessed.

guardian_safety.equipment: One ball or soft substitute; improvised boundary markers.
guardian_safety.environment: Open space clear of hazards and breakables.
guardian_safety.movement_hazards: Running, changes of direction, and object contact. No person-to-person contact is required at any point.
guardian_safety.supervision_note: Guardian confirms space size and whether any second participant is involved.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, described demonstration, or short clip supporting shared rules, fair play, and safe contact limits.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, cue lists, alt text, a transcript, or an adult demonstration. No lesson requires media, and no learner media is ever produced.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose body data, fitness scores, photographs, video, recordings, or comparisons with other learners. For safety-critical units, record only the guardian confirmation that was required.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice or try one safe, optional example of shared rules, fair play, and safe contact limits in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

essential_question: What do all invasion activities have in common once you stop naming the sport?
learning_objectives: Sustain creating and denying space under an unpredictable tactical constraint that forces an immediate decision, using a live opponent when safely available or a solo wall, target, self-pass, or diagrammed sequence that preserves the same decision pressure, holding the critical features when conditions stop being ideal. Full transfer credit requires an immediate tactical decision under changing pressure. A live, solo, or diagrammed route earns equal credit only when the evidence shows the same cue, decision, and recovery response.
Explain what changed about creating and denying space under that demand, and which cue or principle held and which broke down first.
Judge the learner's own creating and denying space against the criteria a second time and account for the difference from the first pass.
success_criteria: The learner holds creating and denying space under an unpredictable tactical constraint that forces an immediate decision, using a live opponent when safely available or a solo wall, target, self-pass, or diagrammed sequence that preserves the same decision pressure, in whatever version their body and setting allow. Full transfer credit requires an immediate tactical decision under changing pressure. A live, solo, or diagrammed route earns equal credit only when the evidence shows the same cue, decision, and recovery response.
The learner names what degraded first and why, rather than reporting only whether it worked.
The learner compares this occasion with the earlier one and says what actually changed.
materials: markers or household objects for boundaries

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Run the space, surface, footwear, and equipment check, then a learner-led warm-up. Restate the stop rule, and name the added demand explicitly before starting: creating and denying space under an unpredictable tactical constraint that forces an immediate decision, using a live opponent when safely available or a solo wall, target, self-pass, or diagrammed sequence that preserves the same decision pressure.

Have the learner restate the critical features of creating and denying space from the earlier pass before any demonstration. Then introduce the transfer condition and ask which feature they expect to lose first, and why. Keep the adapted version available on equal terms.

Work creating and denying space under an unpredictable tactical constraint that forces an immediate decision, using a live opponent when safely available or a solo wall, target, self-pass, or diagrammed sequence that preserves the same decision pressure. Feedback stays on the cue or the decision, never on the learner's body, size, or appearance. Reduce the demand rather than the standard if control breaks down, and say that is the intended response, not a failure.
Learner works creating and denying space independently under the condition at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one.

Cool down, then in one concise response account for the difference between the two occasions of creating and denying space and name the adjustment that carries forward. No recording or photograph is taken.

student_activity: Learner works creating and denying space under an unpredictable tactical constraint that forces an immediate decision, using a live opponent when safely available or a solo wall, target, self-pass, or diagrammed sequence that preserves the same decision pressure at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one. Full transfer credit requires an immediate tactical decision under changing pressure. A live, solo, or diagrammed route earns equal credit only when the evidence shows the same cue, decision, and recovery response.
formative_check: In one concise response, say which feature of creating and denying space degraded first under the added demand, why, and what you would change before the next attempt.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score safe participation, skill cues, tactical reasoning, self-management, and revision. Accept any version of the task the learner’s body and setting allow as full credit when it supplies the stated transfer evidence. Never score body size, weight, body composition, appearance, speed alone, or comparison with another person. Full transfer credit requires an immediate tactical decision under changing pressure. A live, solo, or diagrammed route earns equal credit only when the evidence shows the same cue, decision, and recovery response.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the simplest version of creating and denying space — slower, smaller range, closer target, or seated — then rebuild.
Ask the learner to explain the cue or tactic behind creating and denying space before adding intensity or complexity.
Confirm the specific cue that worked, offer one varied application of creating and denying space, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable movement pattern neutrally, contrast it with the critical features, and schedule varied practice.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: pain, dizziness, breathlessness, or head impact
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Stop immediately, tell an adult, and do not resume in this session. This is never recorded as a failed attempt.

Offer the adapted, seated, solo, or described version of creating and denying space; the alternate route is full credit when it supplies the stated transfer evidence and is not logged as a refusal. Full transfer credit requires an immediate tactical decision under changing pressure. A live, solo, or diagrammed route earns equal credit only when the evidence shows the same cue, decision, and recovery response.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: transfer condition is too much today
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Drop back to the first-pass version of creating and denying space for this session and re-attempt the added demand on a later occasion. Reducing the demand is the correct response and is scored as full participation, but it does not itself satisfy the transfer evidence requirement.
Require accurate independent performance or description plus explanation on a later occasion or in a different setting before marking creating and denying space mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one session. Use safe participation, skill cues, tactical decisions, self-management, personal progress against the learner’s own stated task, and self-assessment — without body-size scoring; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions separated by time or setting.
extension: Design the next progression of creating and denying space yourself, or coach the transfer condition to someone else so that they succeed with it — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.

Activities run in seated, walking, reduced-space, reduced-pace, or no-contact versions. Solo learners use wall, target, and self-pass variants; the tactical understanding, not the game size, is what is assessed.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language about bodies, ability, and effort.
Allow a pause, rest, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Check space, footwear, surface, weather, and equipment before movement.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty, head impact, or unsafe conditions and tell an adult.
Score skill, strategy, self-management, consistency, and reflection — never body size, weight, weight change, body composition, appearance, or comparison with another person.
Do not require weight, BMI, body-fat, body measurement, fitness-test norms, percentile ranks, calorie counts, or diet goals at any point.
Do not require a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as evidence; described, written, and demonstrated-to-one-adult evidence is the intended route.
Do not require performance in front of an audience, a group, or spectators.
The learner may complete the entire unit without another participant, and modifying an activity for access is itself a graded skill rather than a concession.
inclusive_adaptation: Activities run in seated, walking, reduced-space, reduced-pace, or no-contact versions. Solo learners use wall, target, and self-pass variants; the tactical understanding, not the game size, is what is assessed.

guardian_safety.equipment: One ball or soft substitute; improvised boundary markers.
guardian_safety.environment: Open space clear of hazards and breakables.
guardian_safety.movement_hazards: Running, changes of direction, and object contact. No person-to-person contact is required at any point.
guardian_safety.supervision_note: Guardian confirms space size and whether any second participant is involved.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, described demonstration, or short clip supporting creating and denying space.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, cue lists, alt text, a transcript, or an adult demonstration. No lesson requires media, and no learner media is ever produced.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose body data, fitness scores, photographs, video, recordings, or comparisons with other learners. For safety-critical units, record only the guardian confirmation that was required.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice where creating and denying space shows up outside the session under real conditions. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

essential_question: What can movement say that words cannot?
learning_objectives: Sustain dance forms across cultures, treated with accuracy and respect through a complete sequence in which the learner safely pauses when needed and recovers a lost count or interrupted phrase without restarting the evidence from the beginning, holding the critical features when conditions stop being ideal. Full transfer credit requires a complete sequence plus evidence of recovering the count or phrase after an interruption. Performing, notating, storyboarding, or fully describing the sequence earns equal credit, and a safety pause or rest is responsible completion rather than failure.
Explain what changed about dance forms across cultures, treated with accuracy and respect under that demand, and which cue or principle held and which broke down first.
Judge the learner's own dance forms across cultures, treated with accuracy and respect against the criteria a second time and account for the difference from the first pass.
success_criteria: The learner holds dance forms across cultures, treated with accuracy and respect through a complete sequence in which the learner safely pauses when needed and recovers a lost count or interrupted phrase without restarting the evidence from the beginning, in whatever version their body and setting allow. Full transfer credit requires a complete sequence plus evidence of recovering the count or phrase after an interruption. Performing, notating, storyboarding, or fully describing the sequence earns equal credit, and a safety pause or rest is responsible completion rather than failure.
The learner names what degraded first and why, rather than reporting only whether it worked.
The learner compares this occasion with the earlier one and says what actually changed.

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Run the space, surface, footwear, and equipment check, then a learner-led warm-up. Restate the stop rule, and name the added demand explicitly before starting: dance forms across cultures, treated with accuracy and respect through a complete sequence in which the learner safely pauses when needed and recovers a lost count or interrupted phrase without restarting the evidence from the beginning.

Have the learner restate the critical features of dance forms across cultures, treated with accuracy and respect from the earlier pass before any demonstration. Then introduce the transfer condition and ask which feature they expect to lose first, and why. Keep the adapted version available on equal terms.

Work dance forms across cultures, treated with accuracy and respect through a complete sequence in which the learner safely pauses when needed and recovers a lost count or interrupted phrase without restarting the evidence from the beginning. Feedback stays on the cue or the decision, never on the learner's body, size, or appearance. Reduce the demand rather than the standard if control breaks down, and say that is the intended response, not a failure.

Learner works dance forms across cultures, treated with accuracy and respect independently under the condition at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one.

Cool down, then in one concise response account for the difference between the two occasions of dance forms across cultures, treated with accuracy and respect and name the adjustment that carries forward. No recording or photograph is taken.

student_activity: Learner works dance forms across cultures, treated with accuracy and respect through a complete sequence in which the learner safely pauses when needed and recovers a lost count or interrupted phrase without restarting the evidence from the beginning at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one. Full transfer credit requires a complete sequence plus evidence of recovering the count or phrase after an interruption. Performing, notating, storyboarding, or fully describing the sequence earns equal credit, and a safety pause or rest is responsible completion rather than failure.
formative_check: In one concise response, say which feature of dance forms across cultures, treated with accuracy and respect degraded first under the added demand, why, and what you would change before the next attempt.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score safe participation, skill cues, tactical reasoning, self-management, and revision. Accept any version of the task the learner’s body and setting allow as full credit when it supplies the stated transfer evidence. Never score body size, weight, body composition, appearance, speed alone, or comparison with another person. Full transfer credit requires a complete sequence plus evidence of recovering the count or phrase after an interruption. Performing, notating, storyboarding, or fully describing the sequence earns equal credit, and a safety pause or rest is responsible completion rather than failure.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the simplest version of dance forms across cultures, treated with accuracy and respect — slower, smaller range, closer target, or seated — then rebuild.
Ask the learner to explain the cue or tactic behind dance forms across cultures, treated with accuracy and respect before adding intensity or complexity.
Confirm the specific cue that worked, offer one varied application of dance forms across cultures, treated with accuracy and respect, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable movement pattern neutrally, contrast it with the critical features, and schedule varied practice.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: pain, dizziness, breathlessness, or head impact
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Stop immediately, tell an adult, and do not resume in this session. This is never recorded as a failed attempt.

Offer the adapted, seated, solo, or described version of dance forms across cultures, treated with accuracy and respect; the alternate route is full credit when it supplies the stated transfer evidence and is not logged as a refusal. Full transfer credit requires a complete sequence plus evidence of recovering the count or phrase after an interruption. Performing, notating, storyboarding, or fully describing the sequence earns equal credit, and a safety pause or rest is responsible completion rather than failure.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: transfer condition is too much today
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Drop back to the first-pass version of dance forms across cultures, treated with accuracy and respect for this session and re-attempt the added demand on a later occasion. Reducing the demand is the correct response and is scored as full participation, but it does not itself satisfy the transfer evidence requirement.

Require accurate independent performance or description plus explanation on a later occasion or in a different setting before marking dance forms across cultures, treated with accuracy and respect mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one session. Use safe participation, skill cues, tactical decisions, self-management, personal progress against the learner’s own stated task, and self-assessment — without body-size scoring; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions separated by time or setting.
extension: Design the next progression of dance forms across cultures, treated with accuracy and respect yourself, or coach the transfer condition to someone else so that they succeed with it — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
Sequences may be seated, small-range, hand-and-arm only, or built at any tempo. Notation, description, or storyboarding is an accepted alternative to performing.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language about bodies, ability, and effort.
Allow a pause, rest, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Check space, footwear, surface, weather, and equipment before movement.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty, head impact, or unsafe conditions and tell an adult.
Score skill, strategy, self-management, consistency, and reflection — never body size, weight, weight change, body composition, appearance, or comparison with another person.
Do not require weight, BMI, body-fat, body measurement, fitness-test norms, percentile ranks, calorie counts, or diet goals at any point.
Do not require a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as evidence; described, written, and demonstrated-to-one-adult evidence is the intended route.
Do not require performance in front of an audience, a group, or spectators.
No performance is recorded, filmed, photographed, or shown to any audience beyond one trusted adult, and the learner may decline to perform entirely without losing any credit.
inclusive_adaptation: Sequences may be seated, small-range, hand-and-arm only, or built at any tempo. Notation, description, or storyboarding is an accepted alternative to performing.

guardian_safety.equipment: Music source only.
guardian_safety.environment: Clear space with safe flooring.
guardian_safety.movement_hazards: Turning, level changes, and travel. Learner sets range and tempo.
guardian_safety.supervision_note: Guardian confirms who, if anyone, watches; the default is no audience.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, described demonstration, or short clip supporting dance forms across cultures, treated with accuracy and respect.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, cue lists, alt text, a transcript, or an adult demonstration. No lesson requires media, and no learner media is ever produced.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose body data, fitness scores, photographs, video, recordings, or comparisons with other learners. For safety-critical units, record only the guardian confirmation that was required.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice where dance forms across cultures, treated with accuracy and respect shows up outside the session under real conditions. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

essential_question: Which activities would I still be doing at thirty?
learning_objectives: Perform, adapt, or describe yoga, stretching, and mindful movement safely at an intensity, range, and pace the learner sets.
Explain the movement, tactical, or training principle behind yoga, stretching, and mindful movement and why it works.
Self-assess yoga, stretching, and mindful movement against stated criteria and name the next adjustment, without comparing to any other person.
success_criteria: The learner completes or fully describes the yoga, stretching, and mindful movement task using a version their body and setting allow.
The learner gives a cue, principle, tactic, or documented process rather than an unexplained result.
The learner self-assesses against the stated criteria and identifies one next adjustment.
materials: whatever the trialed activities require; free and household options are always offered

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Run the space, surface, footwear, and equipment check, then a learner-led warm-up. Restate the stop rule before any work on yoga, stretching, and mindful movement.

Teach the cues, principle, or tactic behind yoga, stretching, and mindful movement. Demonstrate or describe it, name the critical features, and show at least one adapted version alongside the standard version — not after it.

Practise yoga, stretching, and mindful movement with feedback on cues and decisions only. Feedback addresses the movement or the choice, never the learner's body, size, or appearance. Fade prompting as control improves.
Learner applies yoga, stretching, and mindful movement in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, what they noticed, and what they would adjust.
Cool down, then in one concise response explain the key idea behind yoga, stretching, and mindful movement and name one adjustment for next session. No recording or photograph is taken.

student_activity: Learner applies yoga, stretching, and mindful movement in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, noticed, and would adjust.
formative_check: In one concise response, explain the key idea behind yoga, stretching, and mindful movement and name one adjustment for the next session.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score safe participation, skill cues, tactical reasoning, self-management, and revision. Accept any version of the task the learner’s body and setting allow as full credit. Never score body size, weight, body composition, appearance, speed alone, or comparison with another person.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the simplest version of yoga, stretching, and mindful movement — slower, smaller range, closer target, or seated — then rebuild.
Ask the learner to explain the cue or tactic behind yoga, stretching, and mindful movement before adding intensity or complexity.
Confirm the specific cue that worked, offer one varied application of yoga, stretching, and mindful movement, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable movement pattern neutrally, contrast it with the critical features, and schedule varied practice.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: pain, dizziness, breathlessness, or head impact
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Stop immediately, tell an adult, and do not resume in this session. This is never recorded as a failed attempt.
Offer the adapted, seated, solo, or described version of yoga, stretching, and mindful movement; the alternate route is full credit and is not logged as a refusal.
Require accurate independent performance or description plus explanation on a later occasion or in a different setting before marking yoga, stretching, and mindful movement mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one session. Use safe participation, skill cues, tactical decisions, self-management, personal progress against the learner’s own stated task, and self-assessment — without body-size scoring; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions separated by time or setting.
extension: Apply yoga, stretching, and mindful movement under a new constraint, in a different activity, or teach the cue to someone else — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
Every activity family includes a seated, low-impact, indoor, and zero-cost option, and a learner may design a substitute activity that meets the same description.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language about bodies, ability, and effort.
Allow a pause, rest, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Check space, footwear, surface, weather, and equipment before movement.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty, head impact, or unsafe conditions and tell an adult.
Score skill, strategy, self-management, consistency, and reflection — never body size, weight, weight change, body composition, appearance, or comparison with another person.
Do not require weight, BMI, body-fat, body measurement, fitness-test norms, percentile ranks, calorie counts, or diet goals at any point.
Do not require a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as evidence; described, written, and demonstrated-to-one-adult evidence is the intended route.
Do not require performance in front of an audience, a group, or spectators.
Activity choice is the learner’s. No activity is required that the household cannot access or afford.
inclusive_adaptation: Every activity family includes a seated, low-impact, indoor, and zero-cost option, and a learner may design a substitute activity that meets the same description.

guardian_safety.equipment: Varies by chosen activity; free options are always available.
guardian_safety.environment: Guardian approves any location outside the home.
guardian_safety.movement_hazards: Varies by activity. Guardian approves each trialed activity and its location before it begins.
guardian_safety.supervision_note: Guardian decides supervision level for any activity away from home.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, described demonstration, or short clip supporting yoga, stretching, and mindful movement.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, cue lists, alt text, a transcript, or an adult demonstration. No lesson requires media, and no learner media is ever produced.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose body data, fitness scores, photographs, video, recordings, or comparisons with other learners. For safety-critical units, record only the guardian confirmation that was required.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice or try one safe, optional example of yoga, stretching, and mindful movement in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

essential_question: What does it take to be active outside safely and repeatedly?
learning_objectives: Perform, adapt, or describe hydration, fuel, and pacing for longer outdoor activity safely at an intensity, range, and pace the learner sets.
Explain the movement, tactical, or training principle behind hydration, fuel, and pacing for longer outdoor activity and why it works.
Self-assess hydration, fuel, and pacing for longer outdoor activity against stated criteria and name the next adjustment, without comparing to any other person.
success_criteria: The learner completes or fully describes the hydration, fuel, and pacing for longer outdoor activity task using a version their body and setting allow.
The learner gives a cue, principle, tactic, or documented process rather than an unexplained result.
The learner self-assesses against the stated criteria and identifies one next adjustment.

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Run the space, surface, footwear, and equipment check, then a learner-led warm-up. Restate the stop rule before any work on hydration, fuel, and pacing for longer outdoor activity.

Teach the cues, principle, or tactic behind hydration, fuel, and pacing for longer outdoor activity. Demonstrate or describe it, name the critical features, and show at least one adapted version alongside the standard version — not after it.

Practise hydration, fuel, and pacing for longer outdoor activity with feedback on cues and decisions only. Feedback addresses the movement or the choice, never the learner's body, size, or appearance. Fade prompting as control improves.
Learner applies hydration, fuel, and pacing for longer outdoor activity in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, what they noticed, and what they would adjust.

Cool down, then in one concise response explain the key idea behind hydration, fuel, and pacing for longer outdoor activity and name one adjustment for next session. No recording or photograph is taken.

student_activity: Learner applies hydration, fuel, and pacing for longer outdoor activity in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, noticed, and would adjust.
formative_check: In one concise response, explain the key idea behind hydration, fuel, and pacing for longer outdoor activity and name one adjustment for the next session.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score safe participation, skill cues, tactical reasoning, self-management, and revision. Accept any version of the task the learner’s body and setting allow as full credit. Never score body size, weight, body composition, appearance, speed alone, or comparison with another person.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the simplest version of hydration, fuel, and pacing for longer outdoor activity — slower, smaller range, closer target, or seated — then rebuild.
Ask the learner to explain the cue or tactic behind hydration, fuel, and pacing for longer outdoor activity before adding intensity or complexity.
Confirm the specific cue that worked, offer one varied application of hydration, fuel, and pacing for longer outdoor activity, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable movement pattern neutrally, contrast it with the critical features, and schedule varied practice.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: pain, dizziness, breathlessness, or head impact
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Stop immediately, tell an adult, and do not resume in this session. This is never recorded as a failed attempt.
Offer the adapted, seated, solo, or described version of hydration, fuel, and pacing for longer outdoor activity; the alternate route is full credit and is not logged as a refusal.
Require accurate independent performance or description plus explanation on a later occasion or in a different setting before marking hydration, fuel, and pacing for longer outdoor activity mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one session. Use safe participation, skill cues, tactical decisions, self-management, personal progress against the learner’s own stated task, and self-assessment — without body-size scoring; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions separated by time or setting.
extension: Apply hydration, fuel, and pacing for longer outdoor activity under a new constraint, in a different activity, or teach the cue to someone else — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
Distance, duration, terrain, and pace are learner-set. An indoor or home-yard equivalent is available in full for any learner for whom outdoor activity is unsafe, inaccessible, or not approved.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language about bodies, ability, and effort.
Allow a pause, rest, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Check space, footwear, surface, weather, and equipment before movement.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty, head impact, or unsafe conditions and tell an adult.
Score skill, strategy, self-management, consistency, and reflection — never body size, weight, weight change, body composition, appearance, or comparison with another person.
Do not require weight, BMI, body-fat, body measurement, fitness-test norms, percentile ranks, calorie counts, or diet goals at any point.
Do not require a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as evidence; described, written, and demonstrated-to-one-adult evidence is the intended route.
Do not require performance in front of an audience, a group, or spectators.
The community-space map is built from public information; the learner never records their own route, precise location, or a photograph of themselves.
inclusive_adaptation: Distance, duration, terrain, and pace are learner-set. An indoor or home-yard equivalent is available in full for any learner for whom outdoor activity is unsafe, inaccessible, or not approved.

guardian_safety.equipment: Weather-appropriate clothing and water.
guardian_safety.environment: Outdoor location approved by the guardian, or the indoor equivalent.
guardian_safety.movement_hazards: Traffic, terrain, weather, heat, cold, and sun exposure. Guardian approves the location, route, duration, and supervision before the activity.
guardian_safety.supervision_note: Guardian decides whether the learner is accompanied. No precise location is stored by the course.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, described demonstration, or short clip supporting hydration, fuel, and pacing for longer outdoor activity.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, cue lists, alt text, a transcript, or an adult demonstration. No lesson requires media, and no learner media is ever produced.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose body data, fitness scores, photographs, video, recordings, or comparisons with other learners. For safety-critical units, record only the guardian confirmation that was required.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice or try one safe, optional example of hydration, fuel, and pacing for longer outdoor activity in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

Completing or fully modelling an approved outdoor, home-yard, or indoor scenario earns equal credit when those same planning decisions are evidenced.
The learner names what degraded first and why, rather than reporting only whether it worked.
The learner compares this occasion with the earlier one and says what actually changed.

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Run the space, surface, footwear, and equipment check, then a learner-led warm-up. Restate the stop rule, and name the added demand explicitly before starting: hydration, fuel, and pacing for longer outdoor activity through a guardian-approved outdoor, home-yard, or indoor route scenario where changing weather, terrain, or timing requires the plan to be revised without compromising safety.

Have the learner restate the critical features of hydration, fuel, and pacing for longer outdoor activity from the earlier pass before any demonstration. Then introduce the transfer condition and ask which feature they expect to lose first, and why. Keep the adapted version available on equal terms.

Work hydration, fuel, and pacing for longer outdoor activity through a guardian-approved outdoor, home-yard, or indoor route scenario where changing weather, terrain, or timing requires the plan to be revised without compromising safety. Feedback stays on the cue or the decision, never on the learner's body, size, or appearance. Reduce the demand rather than the standard if control breaks down, and say that is the intended response, not a failure.

Learner works hydration, fuel, and pacing for longer outdoor activity independently under the condition at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one.

Cool down, then in one concise response account for the difference between the two occasions of hydration, fuel, and pacing for longer outdoor activity and name the adjustment that carries forward. No recording or photograph is taken.

student_activity: Learner works hydration, fuel, and pacing for longer outdoor activity through a guardian-approved outdoor, home-yard, or indoor route scenario where changing weather, terrain, or timing requires the plan to be revised without compromising safety at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one. Full transfer credit requires a route plan, a realistic adverse condition, a safe revision, and the reason for that revision. Completing or fully modelling an approved outdoor, home-yard, or indoor scenario earns equal credit when those same planning decisions are evidenced.
formative_check: In one concise response, say which feature of hydration, fuel, and pacing for longer outdoor activity degraded first under the added demand, why, and what you would change before the next attempt.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score safe participation, skill cues, tactical reasoning, self-management, and revision. Accept any version of the task the learner’s body and setting allow as full credit when it supplies the stated transfer evidence. Never score body size, weight, body composition, appearance, speed alone, or comparison with another person. Completing or fully modelling an approved outdoor, home-yard, or indoor scenario earns equal credit when those same planning decisions are evidenced.

Confirm the specific cue that worked, offer one varied application of hydration, fuel, and pacing for longer outdoor activity, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable movement pattern neutrally, contrast it with the critical features, and schedule varied practice.

Completing or fully modelling an approved outdoor, home-yard, or indoor scenario earns equal credit when those same planning decisions are evidenced.

essential_question: What makes an activity one that people actually want to come back to?
learning_objectives: Perform, adapt, or describe winning and losing without changing how you treat people safely at an intensity, range, and pace the learner sets.
Explain the movement, tactical, or training principle behind winning and losing without changing how you treat people and why it works.
Self-assess winning and losing without changing how you treat people against stated criteria and name the next adjustment, without comparing to any other person.
success_criteria: The learner completes or fully describes the winning and losing without changing how you treat people task using a version their body and setting allow.
The learner gives a cue, principle, tactic, or documented process rather than an unexplained result.
The learner self-assesses against the stated criteria and identifies one next adjustment.

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Run the space, surface, footwear, and equipment check, then a learner-led warm-up. Restate the stop rule before any work on winning and losing without changing how you treat people.

Teach the cues, principle, or tactic behind winning and losing without changing how you treat people. Demonstrate or describe it, name the critical features, and show at least one adapted version alongside the standard version — not after it.

Practise winning and losing without changing how you treat people with feedback on cues and decisions only. Feedback addresses the movement or the choice, never the learner's body, size, or appearance. Fade prompting as control improves.
Learner applies winning and losing without changing how you treat people in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, what they noticed, and what they would adjust.

Cool down, then in one concise response explain the key idea behind winning and losing without changing how you treat people and name one adjustment for next session. No recording or photograph is taken.

student_activity: Learner applies winning and losing without changing how you treat people in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, noticed, and would adjust.
formative_check: In one concise response, explain the key idea behind winning and losing without changing how you treat people and name one adjustment for the next session.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score safe participation, skill cues, tactical reasoning, self-management, and revision. Accept any version of the task the learner’s body and setting allow as full credit. Never score body size, weight, body composition, appearance, speed alone, or comparison with another person.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the simplest version of winning and losing without changing how you treat people — slower, smaller range, closer target, or seated — then rebuild.
Ask the learner to explain the cue or tactic behind winning and losing without changing how you treat people before adding intensity or complexity.
Confirm the specific cue that worked, offer one varied application of winning and losing without changing how you treat people, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable movement pattern neutrally, contrast it with the critical features, and schedule varied practice.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: pain, dizziness, breathlessness, or head impact
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Stop immediately, tell an adult, and do not resume in this session. This is never recorded as a failed attempt.
Offer the adapted, seated, solo, or described version of winning and losing without changing how you treat people; the alternate route is full credit and is not logged as a refusal.

Require accurate independent performance or description plus explanation on a later occasion or in a different setting before marking winning and losing without changing how you treat people mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one session. Use safe participation, skill cues, tactical decisions, self-management, personal progress against the learner’s own stated task, and self-assessment — without body-size scoring; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions separated by time or setting.
extension: Apply winning and losing without changing how you treat people under a new constraint, in a different activity, or teach the cue to someone else — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
The redesign may be written, diagrammed, described aloud, or trialed practically. Practical trial is optional.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language about bodies, ability, and effort.
Allow a pause, rest, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Check space, footwear, surface, weather, and equipment before movement.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty, head impact, or unsafe conditions and tell an adult.
Score skill, strategy, self-management, consistency, and reflection — never body size, weight, weight change, body composition, appearance, or comparison with another person.
Do not require weight, BMI, body-fat, body measurement, fitness-test norms, percentile ranks, calorie counts, or diet goals at any point.
Do not require a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as evidence; described, written, and demonstrated-to-one-adult evidence is the intended route.
Do not require performance in front of an audience, a group, or spectators.
This unit makes inclusive design an assessed competency in its own right rather than an accommodation applied to someone else.
inclusive_adaptation: The redesign may be written, diagrammed, described aloud, or trialed practically. Practical trial is optional.

guardian_safety.equipment: Reuses equipment from earlier units.
guardian_safety.environment: Indoor study space; practical trial optional.
guardian_safety.movement_hazards: None required.
guardian_safety.supervision_note: No additional supervision needed for the written redesign.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, described demonstration, or short clip supporting winning and losing without changing how you treat people.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, cue lists, alt text, a transcript, or an adult demonstration. No lesson requires media, and no learner media is ever produced.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose body data, fitness scores, photographs, video, recordings, or comparisons with other learners. For safety-critical units, record only the guardian confirmation that was required.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice or try one safe, optional example of winning and losing without changing how you treat people in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

essential_question: What can I now do, and what am I choosing to carry forward?
learning_objectives: Perform, adapt, or describe explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words safely at an intensity, range, and pace the learner sets.
Explain the movement, tactical, or training principle behind explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words and why it works.
Self-assess explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words against stated criteria and name the next adjustment, without comparing to any other person.
success_criteria: The learner completes or fully describes the explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words task using a version their body and setting allow.
The learner gives a cue, principle, tactic, or documented process rather than an unexplained result.
The learner self-assesses against the stated criteria and identifies one next adjustment.
materials: the year’s course notebook or digital equivalent

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Run the space, surface, footwear, and equipment check, then a learner-led warm-up. Restate the stop rule before any work on explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words.

Teach the cues, principle, or tactic behind explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words. Demonstrate or describe it, name the critical features, and show at least one adapted version alongside the standard version — not after it.

Practise explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words with feedback on cues and decisions only. Feedback addresses the movement or the choice, never the learner's body, size, or appearance. Fade prompting as control improves.

Learner applies explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, what they noticed, and what they would adjust.

Cool down, then in one concise response explain the key idea behind explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words and name one adjustment for next session. No recording or photograph is taken.

student_activity: Learner applies explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, noticed, and would adjust.
formative_check: In one concise response, explain the key idea behind explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words and name one adjustment for the next session.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score safe participation, skill cues, tactical reasoning, self-management, and revision. Accept any version of the task the learner’s body and setting allow as full credit. Never score body size, weight, body composition, appearance, speed alone, or comparison with another person.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the simplest version of explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words — slower, smaller range, closer target, or seated — then rebuild.
Ask the learner to explain the cue or tactic behind explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words before adding intensity or complexity.
Confirm the specific cue that worked, offer one varied application of explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable movement pattern neutrally, contrast it with the critical features, and schedule varied practice.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: pain, dizziness, breathlessness, or head impact
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Stop immediately, tell an adult, and do not resume in this session. This is never recorded as a failed attempt.
Offer the adapted, seated, solo, or described version of explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words; the alternate route is full credit and is not logged as a refusal.

Require accurate independent performance or description plus explanation on a later occasion or in a different setting before marking explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one session. Use safe participation, skill cues, tactical decisions, self-management, personal progress against the learner’s own stated task, and self-assessment — without body-size scoring; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions separated by time or setting.
extension: Apply explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words under a new constraint, in a different activity, or teach the cue to someone else — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
Presentation may be spoken one-to-one, written, or submitted as an annotated document. No recording, video, photograph, or audience beyond one adult is required.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language about bodies, ability, and effort.
Allow a pause, rest, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Check space, footwear, surface, weather, and equipment before movement.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty, head impact, or unsafe conditions and tell an adult.
Score skill, strategy, self-management, consistency, and reflection — never body size, weight, weight change, body composition, appearance, or comparison with another person.
Do not require weight, BMI, body-fat, body measurement, fitness-test norms, percentile ranks, calorie counts, or diet goals at any point.
Do not require a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as evidence; described, written, and demonstrated-to-one-adult evidence is the intended route.
Do not require performance in front of an audience, a group, or spectators.
Portfolio evidence is described in words; no photographic or video proof of any performance is requested or accepted as a requirement.
inclusive_adaptation: Presentation may be spoken one-to-one, written, or submitted as an annotated document. No recording, video, photograph, or audience beyond one adult is required.

guardian_safety.equipment: None.
guardian_safety.environment: Indoor space for a one-to-one review.
guardian_safety.movement_hazards: None expected.
guardian_safety.supervision_note: Guardian acts as reviewer. The review is a conversation, not a recorded artifact.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, described demonstration, or short clip supporting explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, cue lists, alt text, a transcript, or an adult demonstration. No lesson requires media, and no learner media is ever produced.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose body data, fitness scores, photographs, video, recordings, or comparisons with other learners. For safety-critical units, record only the guardian confirmation that was required.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice or try one safe, optional example of explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.
