essential_question: What can I now do, and what am I choosing to carry forward?
learning_objectives: Perform, adapt, or describe reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use safely at an intensity, range, and pace the learner sets.
Explain the movement, tactical, or training principle behind reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use and why it works.
Self-assess reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use against stated criteria and name the next adjustment, without comparing to any other person.
success_criteria: The learner completes or fully describes the reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use task using a version their body and setting allow.
The learner gives a cue, principle, tactic, or documented process rather than an unexplained result.
The learner self-assesses against the stated criteria and identifies one next adjustment.
materials: the year’s course notebook or digital equivalent

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Run the space, surface, footwear, and equipment check, then a learner-led warm-up. Restate the stop rule before any work on reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use.

Teach the cues, principle, or tactic behind reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use. Demonstrate or describe it, name the critical features, and show at least one adapted version alongside the standard version — not after it.

Practise reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use with feedback on cues and decisions only. Feedback addresses the movement or the choice, never the learner's body, size, or appearance. Fade prompting as control improves.
Learner applies reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, what they noticed, and what they would adjust.

Cool down, then in one concise response explain the key idea behind reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use and name one adjustment for next session. No recording or photograph is taken.

student_activity: Learner applies reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, noticed, and would adjust.
formative_check: In one concise response, explain the key idea behind reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use and name one adjustment for the next session.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score safe participation, skill cues, tactical reasoning, self-management, and revision. Accept any version of the task the learner’s body and setting allow as full credit. Never score body size, weight, body composition, appearance, speed alone, or comparison with another person.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the simplest version of reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use — slower, smaller range, closer target, or seated — then rebuild.
Ask the learner to explain the cue or tactic behind reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use before adding intensity or complexity.
Confirm the specific cue that worked, offer one varied application of reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable movement pattern neutrally, contrast it with the critical features, and schedule varied practice.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: pain, dizziness, breathlessness, or head impact
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Stop immediately, tell an adult, and do not resume in this session. This is never recorded as a failed attempt.
Offer the adapted, seated, solo, or described version of reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use; the alternate route is full credit and is not logged as a refusal.

Require accurate independent performance or description plus explanation on a later occasion or in a different setting before marking reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one session. Use safe participation, skill cues, tactical decisions, self-management, personal progress against the learner’s own stated task, and self-assessment — without body-size scoring; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions separated by time or setting.
extension: Apply reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use under a new constraint, in a different activity, or teach the cue to someone else — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
Presentation may be spoken one-to-one, written, or submitted as an annotated document. No recording, video, photograph, or audience beyond one adult is required.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language about bodies, ability, and effort.
Allow a pause, rest, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Check space, footwear, surface, weather, and equipment before movement.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty, head impact, or unsafe conditions and tell an adult.
Score skill, strategy, self-management, consistency, and reflection — never body size, weight, weight change, body composition, appearance, or comparison with another person.
Do not require weight, BMI, body-fat, body measurement, fitness-test norms, percentile ranks, calorie counts, or diet goals at any point.
Do not require a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as evidence; described, written, and demonstrated-to-one-adult evidence is the intended route.
Do not require performance in front of an audience, a group, or spectators.
Portfolio evidence is described in words; no photographic or video proof of any performance is requested or accepted as a requirement.
inclusive_adaptation: Presentation may be spoken one-to-one, written, or submitted as an annotated document. No recording, video, photograph, or audience beyond one adult is required.

guardian_safety.equipment: None.
guardian_safety.environment: Indoor space for a one-to-one review.
guardian_safety.movement_hazards: None expected.
guardian_safety.supervision_note: Guardian acts as reviewer. The review is a conversation, not a recorded artifact.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, described demonstration, or short clip supporting reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, cue lists, alt text, a transcript, or an adult demonstration. No lesson requires media, and no learner media is ever produced.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose body data, fitness scores, photographs, video, recordings, or comparisons with other learners. For safety-critical units, record only the guardian confirmation that was required.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice or try one safe, optional example of reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

Explain what changed about explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words under that demand, and which cue or principle held and which broke down first.
Judge the learner's own explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words against the criteria a second time and account for the difference from the first pass.
success_criteria: The learner holds explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words assembled into the portfolio itself and defended against a question the learner did not prepare for, in whatever version their body and setting allow.

materials: the year’s course notebook or digital equivalent

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Run the space, surface, footwear, and equipment check, then a learner-led warm-up. Restate the stop rule, and name the added demand explicitly before starting: explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words assembled into the portfolio itself and defended against a question the learner did not prepare for.

Have the learner restate the critical features of explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words from the earlier pass before any demonstration. Then introduce the transfer condition and ask which feature they expect to lose first, and why. Keep the adapted version available on equal terms.

Work explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words assembled into the portfolio itself and defended against a question the learner did not prepare for. Feedback stays on the cue or the decision, never on the learner's body, size, or appearance. Reduce the demand rather than the standard if control breaks down, and say that is the intended response, not a failure.

Learner works explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words independently under the condition at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one.

Cool down, then in one concise response account for the difference between the two occasions of explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words and name the adjustment that carries forward. No recording or photograph is taken.

student_activity: Learner works explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words assembled into the portfolio itself and defended against a question the learner did not prepare for at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one.
formative_check: In one concise response, say which feature of explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words degraded first under the added demand, why, and what you would change before the next attempt.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score safe participation, skill cues, tactical reasoning, self-management, and revision. Accept any version of the task the learner’s body and setting allow as full credit. Never score body size, weight, body composition, appearance, speed alone, or comparison with another person.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the simplest version of explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words — slower, smaller range, closer target, or seated — then rebuild.
Ask the learner to explain the cue or tactic behind explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words before adding intensity or complexity.
Confirm the specific cue that worked, offer one varied application of explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable movement pattern neutrally, contrast it with the critical features, and schedule varied practice.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: pain, dizziness, breathlessness, or head impact
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Stop immediately, tell an adult, and do not resume in this session. This is never recorded as a failed attempt.
Offer the adapted, seated, solo, or described version of explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words; the alternate route is full credit and is not logged as a refusal.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: transfer condition is too much today
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Drop back to the first-pass version of explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words for this session and re-attempt the added demand on a later occasion. Reducing the demand is the correct response and is scored as full participation.

Require accurate independent performance or description plus explanation on a later occasion or in a different setting before marking explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one session. Use safe participation, skill cues, tactical decisions, self-management, personal progress against the learner’s own stated task, and self-assessment — without body-size scoring; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions separated by time or setting.
extension: Design the next progression of explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words yourself, or coach the transfer condition to someone else so that they succeed with it — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
Presentation may be spoken one-to-one, written, or submitted as an annotated document. No recording, video, photograph, or audience beyond one adult is required.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language about bodies, ability, and effort.
Allow a pause, rest, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Check space, footwear, surface, weather, and equipment before movement.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty, head impact, or unsafe conditions and tell an adult.
Score skill, strategy, self-management, consistency, and reflection — never body size, weight, weight change, body composition, appearance, or comparison with another person.
Do not require weight, BMI, body-fat, body measurement, fitness-test norms, percentile ranks, calorie counts, or diet goals at any point.
Do not require a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as evidence; described, written, and demonstrated-to-one-adult evidence is the intended route.
Do not require performance in front of an audience, a group, or spectators.
Portfolio evidence is described in words; no photographic or video proof of any performance is requested or accepted as a requirement.
inclusive_adaptation: Presentation may be spoken one-to-one, written, or submitted as an annotated document. No recording, video, photograph, or audience beyond one adult is required.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, described demonstration, or short clip supporting explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, cue lists, alt text, a transcript, or an adult demonstration. No lesson requires media, and no learner media is ever produced.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. home_connection: Invite the learner to notice where explaining a tactical or training principle in the learner’s own words shows up outside the session under real conditions. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

essential_question: What can I now do, and what am I choosing to carry forward?
learning_objectives: Sustain reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use assembled into the portfolio itself and defended against a question the learner did not prepare for, holding the critical features when conditions stop being ideal.
Explain what changed about reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use under that demand, and which cue or principle held and which broke down first.
Judge the learner's own reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use against the criteria a second time and account for the difference from the first pass.
success_criteria: The learner holds reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use assembled into the portfolio itself and defended against a question the learner did not prepare for, in whatever version their body and setting allow.
The learner names what degraded first and why, rather than reporting only whether it worked.
The learner compares this occasion with the earlier one and says what actually changed.
materials: the year’s course notebook or digital equivalent

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Run the space, surface, footwear, and equipment check, then a learner-led warm-up. Restate the stop rule, and name the added demand explicitly before starting: reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use assembled into the portfolio itself and defended against a question the learner did not prepare for.

Have the learner restate the critical features of reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use from the earlier pass before any demonstration. Then introduce the transfer condition and ask which feature they expect to lose first, and why. Keep the adapted version available on equal terms.

Work reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use assembled into the portfolio itself and defended against a question the learner did not prepare for. Feedback stays on the cue or the decision, never on the learner's body, size, or appearance. Reduce the demand rather than the standard if control breaks down, and say that is the intended response, not a failure.

Learner works reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use independently under the condition at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one.

Cool down, then in one concise response account for the difference between the two occasions of reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use and name the adjustment that carries forward. No recording or photograph is taken.

student_activity: Learner works reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use assembled into the portfolio itself and defended against a question the learner did not prepare for at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one.
formative_check: In one concise response, say which feature of reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use degraded first under the added demand, why, and what you would change before the next attempt.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score safe participation, skill cues, tactical reasoning, self-management, and revision. Accept any version of the task the learner’s body and setting allow as full credit. Never score body size, weight, body composition, appearance, speed alone, or comparison with another person.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the simplest version of reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use — slower, smaller range, closer target, or seated — then rebuild.
Ask the learner to explain the cue or tactic behind reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use before adding intensity or complexity.
Confirm the specific cue that worked, offer one varied application of reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable movement pattern neutrally, contrast it with the critical features, and schedule varied practice.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: pain, dizziness, breathlessness, or head impact
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Stop immediately, tell an adult, and do not resume in this session. This is never recorded as a failed attempt.
Offer the adapted, seated, solo, or described version of reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use; the alternate route is full credit and is not logged as a refusal.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: transfer condition is too much today
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Drop back to the first-pass version of reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use for this session and re-attempt the added demand on a later occasion. Reducing the demand is the correct response and is scored as full participation.

Require accurate independent performance or description plus explanation on a later occasion or in a different setting before marking reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one session. Use safe participation, skill cues, tactical decisions, self-management, personal progress against the learner’s own stated task, and self-assessment — without body-size scoring; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions separated by time or setting.
extension: Design the next progression of reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use yourself, or coach the transfer condition to someone else so that they succeed with it — without completing another learner's graded work.
